slides.title: 1 · System Diagram

shapes.text:
MCP servers (built by us, running on the RPi):
asr-mcp · tts-mcp · task-mcp · tools-mcp
files · commands · time · weather · system stats · reminders · notes · telegram

Boundary: audio + VAD + MCP servers on-device;
LLM inference in the cloud

slides.notes: One diagram: audio path, MCP servers, cloud boundary, barge-in.

slides.title: 1b · Audio path & barge-in behavior
bullets: Local audio transport keeps the microphone open during playback (full-duplex)
VAD: Silero on-device @16 kHz — confidence 0.75, start 0.3 s, stop 0.8 s
Turn end: Local Smart-Turn v3 (ONNX) + 0.8 s stop window
Echo: PipeWire module-echo-cancel (WebRTC AEC, suppression level 2) — TTS plays through the AEC sink, mic reads the AEC source
Second layer: in-process echo detector — cross-correlation + spectral-envelope vote against the played TTS audio
Barge-in: user speech → cancel TTS playback, stop the LLM stream, listen immediately
All stage timings recorded on one monotonic clock and streamed to the live dashboard
slides.notes: Emphasize: mic never muted; AEC + detector keep self-hearing out.

slides.title: 2 · System Prompt (v1) — versioned in repo

bullets.text: "You are a friendly assistant running on a Raspberry Pi 5. Keep spoken answers short (1-3 sentences)..."
Use MCP tools: get_time, search_web, get_weather, system_stats, reminders, notes, telegram
"Never read a tool's raw output aloud — work results into a natural sentence"
"Think silently... output ONLY the final answer sentence(s)" + 'Detailed thinking: off.'
"Never publish anything to GitHub unless the user explicitly approves in this conversation"
Model: nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free via OpenRouter — thinking disabled (reasoning.enabled=false)

slides.notes: v1 changelog: thinking disabled after TTS leak; approval gating for publishing.

bullets.text: MCP tool results (time, weather, search, files, stats)
pipecat LLMContext: rolling window, trims old turns
State machine: idle → listen → think → speak

slides.title: 5 · Evaluation & Benchmark — method
bullets: One clock: monotonic timestamps on every stage; JSON + CSV per run
Chain: VAD end → ASR final → LLM first token → TTS first audio → speaker
E2E = speaker − VAD end; barge-in = playback-stop − speech start
8 phrases × 3 runs = 24 text-injected turns (automated via dashboard)
6 human-spoken turns captured for the voice-side stages
All runs on the deployed RPi 5 agent over Wi-Fi LAN
benchmark/remote_bench.py · benchmark/voice_reconstruct.py · benchmark/wer_test.py
slides.notes: Everything automated from the live dashboard event log.

slides.title: 6 · Demo (2-3 min, live on the RPi)
bullets: 1. Walk up and just SPEAK — no push-to-talk: "What time is it in New York?"
2. Natural follow-up while it answers — barge-in cuts playback instantly
3. Live MCP tool call: "What's the weather in Manila?" (Open-Meteo)
4. Background agent: "Build me a small portfolio website" → task id → spoken progress announcements
5. Ask for task status while it runs — agent stays conversational
6. Dashboard on a laptop: per-stage latency chips, tool calls, activity timeline
7. Recovery: disconnect/reconnect network mid-chat — agent recovers gracefully

slides.title: Challenges → Fixes → Proof

rows: Agent heard its own TTS and answered itself (loops)
Root cause chain: wrong pipecat frame class + ALSA bypassing PipeWire; fixed routing, added PipeWire WebRTC AEC (suppression 2) + correlation/spectral echo detector
Echo decisions logged live; ghost turns: 3-4 per response → 0
Chain-of-thought leaked into spoken answers mid-tool-loop
Disabled thinking (reasoning.enabled=false) + 'Detailed thinking: off' prompt + dashboard text guard
Tool-result turn: 3.5 s → 0.9 s; no narration since
pipecat direct functions must deliver via result_callback — fixed all 16 tools
All tools return values live (time, weather, search, files…)
Mic muted during TTS killed barge-in
Replaced the mute-gate with AEC + echo detector — mic always open
Barge-in works; interruption latency recorded on the dashboard

slides.notes: Each row: challenge, engineering fix, and the measurement that proves it.
